purpose: How a website-and-hosting reseller decides what fixed-scope site build plus monthly care plan to sell and to which local niche, derives both prices from its own measured cost ledger instead of invented market rates, wins and compounds clients through honest proof, evidence-first outreach, referral loops and disclosed partner introductions, and qualifies, scopes and expectation-sets every deal so the promised work, the client's ownership of their own domain and content, and the honest limits of what a website can do are all fixed in writing before a build begins.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a solo or very small shop selling to local small businesses (owner-operated trades, clinics, restaurants, studios) where the buyer is usually the owner and the decision is made in one or two conversations
revenue has two legs, a one-time build fee and a recurring care plan, and the business only compounds if the recurring leg survives well past the first year
every price in this KB is a mechanism: a way to derive a number from the operator's own measured time and costs and to verify it deal by deal, never a market rate recalled from somewhere else

the operator's jurisdiction governs contracts, cancellation rights, recurring billing, unsolicited commercial contact and accessibility duties; those obligation classes are named here and the operator verifies current rules in their own jurisdiction
exclusions: choosing the build stack and design system and running the standardized build pipeline from content intake through launch, which belongs to the site-build-and-delivery KB this one hands off to
quality, performance and accessibility baselines and the technical launch checklist, including domain, DNS and email cutover mechanics, which belong to the site-build-and-delivery KB

hosting architecture for a portfolio of sites, backup, update and security operations, monthly value reporting, retention, reactivation and offboarding handover, which belong to the hosting-care-plan-and-retention KB; this KB covers only what the care plan promises at the moment of sale and how its price is derived

invented market rates, benchmark prices, commission percentages or typical monthly figures of any kind; every number here is a derived mechanism or a qualitative band the operator computes from its own records
search-ranking or traffic guarantees, lead-volume or revenue promises, SEO campaign work and paid-advertising management, and any performance claim that cannot be measured on the client's own site
holding a client's domain, DNS, content, site files or form inbox as commercial leverage; the ownership pledge forbids it and no acquisition or retention tactic in this KB may depend on it

personalized legal, tax, accounting or financial advice to the client or to the operator; contract, consumer-protection, commercial-contact and accessibility points name the obligation class and direct the operator to verify current rules in their jurisdiction
hiring, subcontractor management and agency scaling beyond the solo or very-small-shop frame this KB assumes

glossary.definition: A fixed deliverable set sold at a stated price under stated conditions so that every sale is the same product rather than a fresh estimate; variation is absorbed by a short add-on list instead of by re-scoping each deal from a blank page.

The recurring leg of the offer: monthly custody of a working site, typically hosting and domain administration, backups, platform and plugin updates, security and uptime checking and a bounded allowance of small edits. What it promises is decided here; how the work is operated month to month belongs to the hosting-care-plan-and-retention KB.

The lowest price at which a deliverable does not lose money, assembled from measured build time valued at the rate the operator needs their hours to earn, third-party pass-through costs, a rework reserve and a share of unbilled selling and admin time. It is derived from the operator's own ledger and never copied from an advertised price.

The bounded amount of small-change work included in a care plan each month, expressed as a time budget or a request count with a written definition of what counts as small, so that the phrase 'updates included' has an honest edge and an overflow path.

The accumulation of small out-of-scope requests absorbed without a change order, each individually reasonable, which together convert a fixed-price build into unpaid hourly work and quietly reset what the client believes the care plan includes.

A short written record naming an out-of-scope request, the basis on which it is priced and its effect on the launch date, agreed before the work is done, and written even when the agreed price is zero.

An openly disclosed, time-bounded reduced price offered to early clients in exchange for something received in return, usually a reference or case-study permission; it stays above pass-through cost and is never presented as the standing price.

The self-feeding acquisition pattern in which a delivered site produces a satisfied owner who introduces peers in the same trade, which produces another site; its strength depends on the moment of the ask, how easy the introduction is to pass on, and whether the delivery was worth talking about.

A statement about what the site does that names what is measured, on which page and with what tool, so the client can re-check it themselves; anything that cannot be stated that way is not claimed in a proposal, a portfolio item or an outreach message.

The standing written commitment that the client's domain registration, content, images, site files and form inbox belong to the client and are handed over on request, so that retention has to be earned by service quality rather than by controlling access.

nodes.definition: Decide, before any pricing or prospecting, that the thing for sale is a package and not an estimate: one fixed-scope small-business website plus one monthly care plan, quoted together and delivered the same way every time. This is the decision that separates this business from freelance web work, because a freelancer sells hours against a brief that keeps moving while a productized shop sells a known deliverable whose build cost falls as it is repeated and whose recurring leg turns every finished site into an annuity. The thesis fixes three commitments that everything downstream inherits: the same deliverable list on every deal, both revenue legs presented in the same breath so the monthly fee is never a late surprise, and any request outside the package handled as a named add-on or an honest decline rather than a quiet re-scope.

included: the decision that the package rather than the hour is the unit of sale
the commitment to present build fee and care plan together
the rule that misfits become add-ons or declines

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the closed-deal mix shows the standard package being bent or the monthly leg being dropped on most sales

pros.claim: Repetition on one deliverable turns build time into a falling cost and quoting into a short conversation
pros.example: the third landscaper site reuses the page structure and intake questions worked out on the first, so the quote becomes a page count and a start date instead of a two-day estimating exercise

pros.claim: Quoting both legs together makes the recurring revenue a normal part of the product rather than something that has to be sold again later
pros.example: a bakery owner agreeing to the monthly plan in the same conversation as the build because the two were never presented separately

cons.claim: A fixed package forfeits paying work that a bespoke shop would happily take
cons.example: turning down a booking-and-payments build for a yoga studio because the package sells a brochure site with an inquiry form

failure_modes: calling the offer a package while still quoting every deal from scratch, so nothing ever becomes cheaper to build
defining the package around the tools the operator enjoys rather than what the target buyer needs
presenting the build fee first and the monthly plan afterwards, which makes the recurring leg feel like a bait-and-switch
acceptance_tests: the offer can be stated on one page: what is delivered, what is not, what recurs monthly, and where an add-on price comes from
two different prospects in the target niche can be quoted from the same sheet without any new estimating
revisit_triggers: several consecutive deals need an out-of-package build in order to close
the recurring leg is being dropped from proposals in order to win the build fee

nodes.definition: Choose which kind of local business the offer aims at, judged on operator-relevant tests rather than on which trade sounds appealing. The tests are whether the same site structure genuinely repeats across the trade (a roofer, a plumber and an electrician need near-identical pages, while every restaurant needs a menu that changes weekly), whether the owners already believe a website matters for the work they do, whether enough of them are reachable inside a drivable service area and cluster in suppliers, associations and job sites where a reputation travels, and whether the buyer has a business reason to keep paying every month once the site is live. The choice is a bet to be re-read against recorded conversion evidence, not a permanent identity; the two practical failures are a niche so narrow the local pool empties within a year and one so wide that nothing about the second build is cheaper than the first.

included: the fit tests for a candidate trade
qualitative reading of reachable local density and where the trade clusters
the rule that the niche decision is re-read on recorded evidence
excluded: the pitch used on that niche
any claim about market size in figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recorded outreach and referral results by trade show a different vertical converting or the current one drying up

pros.claim: A niche whose site structure repeats compounds every asset the operator owns, from intake questions to objection answers
pros.example: the fourth heating-and-cooling site reusing the service-area page pattern and the seasonal tune-up call-to-action proven on the first three

cons.claim: Narrowing concentrates the whole business in one trade's fortunes and one network's opinion of you
cons.example: a single unhappy contractor speaking at the trade association's monthly meeting closing an entire channel at once

cons.claim: A niche chosen before there is any conversion evidence is a guess that costs a full outreach cycle to test
cons.example: committing the demonstration build and the sales language to one trade and learning only weeks later that its owners never answer the phone

failure_modes: choosing a trade because its businesses look prosperous rather than because their sites repeat
picking owners who are unreachable during working hours and never adapting the contact method
staying in a niche after the local pool is visibly exhausted because the assets were built for it
acceptance_tests: the chosen niche is written down with each fit test answered, including where its owners gather
at least one repeatable page structure and one recurring objection are identified before outreach starts
revisit_triggers: conversion in the chosen niche stalls across a full outreach cycle
the referral network inside the niche stops producing introductions

nodes.definition: Work out what a small-business owner is actually hiring a website to do, because the answer is rarely 'a website'. The recurring jobs are legitimacy (someone who was given their name looks them up and has to see a real business), being findable for their own name with the immediate facts attached (hours, service area, phone, directions), a contact route that does not depend on the owner answering a phone from a ladder, replacement of something broken or embarrassing (a dead site, an expired domain, a page unusable on a phone), and escape from a previous vendor who stopped answering. Diagnosing which job is live for this particular buyer decides the pitch, the page structure and the proof worth showing, and it is also what tells the operator when the honest answer is that a website is not this owner's problem at all.

included: the recurring jobs a local site is hired to do
diagnosing which job is live for this buyer from their own words
recognising when a site is not the buyer's real problem
excluded: the claims the operator is allowed to make about outcomes
traffic or keyword analysis of any kind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the jobs prospects describe in intake calls diverge from the ones the offer is built around

pros.claim: Naming the live job makes the pitch short and concrete because it describes something the owner already feels
pros.example: showing an owner that their current page is unreadable on a phone answers the job in one gesture, without a word about rankings

cons.claim: The stated job and the real job often differ, and correcting an owner out loud can feel like being told they are wrong
cons.example: an owner who asks to be first on Google when what they need is a site that loads and shows accurate opening hours

failure_modes: accepting 'I want more customers' as the job and inheriting an outcome no website alone can deliver
diagnosing from the operator's taste rather than from the buyer's words and their current page
using the diagnosis to manufacture anxiety instead of to describe an observable problem
acceptance_tests: the proposal names the specific job in the owner's own words together with the observable evidence for it
the operator can state at least one case in this niche where the honest answer is that a website will not fix the problem
revisit_triggers: prospects in the niche consistently describe a job the current pitch does not address
the same misdiagnosis appears in two projects that ended unhappily

nodes.definition: Fix, as a standing rule of the business, the line between what a website demonstrably does and what may never be promised. On the demonstrable side sit facts the operator can show on the client's own site and re-measure later: the site exists and works on a phone, page speed and correctness can be measured before and after with a named tool, the business name, hours, service area and contact route are present and accurate, inquiries arrive at an address the owner controls, and the site can be found when its own business name is searched. Off the table are guarantees about search ranking, traffic volume, lead counts or revenue, all of which depend on competitors, platform behaviour and the client's own follow-up. Every performance claim must name what is measured, on which page and with what tool, so the client can re-check it; a claim that cannot be stated that way is simply not made, in a proposal, a portfolio item or an outreach message.

included: the demonstrable-versus-promised line
the requirement that any performance claim names its measurement
the refusal of ranking, traffic, lead and revenue guarantees
excluded: the technical measurement baseline of a build, which the delivery KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sales document, portfolio item or client conversation is found carrying a claim that cannot name its measurement

pros.claim: Refusing guarantees removes the single promise most likely to end in a refund demand and a bad word inside a tight niche
pros.example: declining to promise a first-page position and instead showing a measured before-and-after load time on the client's own pages

cons.claim: Competitors who do promise rankings will sometimes win the deal on the strength of the promise alone
cons.example: losing a dental practice to a vendor guaranteeing page one within ninety days, a promise the operator will not match

failure_modes: softening a refused guarantee into an implication such as 'clients usually see more calls' that the buyer hears as a promise
quoting a performance number with no stated measurement method or tool
letting a case study imply that the new site caused a revenue jump the client never attributed to it
acceptance_tests: every claim in the proposal, the portfolio and the operator's own site names what is measured, where, and how the client can re-check it
no document in the sales kit contains a ranking, traffic, lead-count or revenue guarantee, explicit or implied
revisit_triggers: a client repeats back an outcome expectation nobody promised
a case study or testimonial starts implying a result the operator cannot verify

nodes.definition: Commit in writing, before the first invoice, that the things which are the client's remain the client's: the domain registered in the client's name or in an account they can take over, the text and photographs they supplied, the site files and database, and the inbox that receives form submissions. The operator may administer all of it as a service but never hold it as leverage: access is handed over on request, the exit path is documented at the moment of sale rather than at the moment of departure, and no cancellation clause is allowed to make a client's own address unreachable. This is simultaneously an ethical line and a commercial position, because it answers the buyer's most common and best-founded fear, being trapped by a vendor again, and because it forces the business to retain clients on the quality of the service instead of on the cost of leaving.

included: registrar and account ownership in the client's name
the written exit path stated at sale time
the rule that no term or practice turns client assets into leverage
excluded: the mechanics of transferring a domain or migrating a site, owned by the delivery KB
offboarding execution and the handover procedure, owned by the care-plan KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a registrar, platform or payment provider changes how ownership, access or transfers work, or a departure reveals an unassigned asset

pros.claim: The ownership promise answers the objection that kills the most deals in this trade, which is having been burned by the last web person
pros.example: an owner whose previous developer vanished with the registrar login signing the same week the transfer path is shown to them in writing

cons.claim: Client-held ownership means any client can leave at any time with everything, and some will
cons.example: a client of two years moving the site to a relative and taking the domain, content and form inbox with them in an afternoon

failure_modes: registering the client's domain inside the operator's own account for convenience and creating leverage nobody intended
documenting the exit path nowhere, so an amicable departure turns into a dispute
quietly relying on a client's inability to leave when service quality slips
acceptance_tests: the signed scope names who holds the domain, the content and the site files and what happens to each on cancellation
a client can be shown at any time the exact steps by which they would take everything and go
revisit_triggers: a registrar or platform changes how account ownership or transfers work
a cancellation exposes an asset that nobody had assigned an owner to

nodes.definition: Bind every sales conversation to conduct that survives the client repeating it word for word to their peers. The rules are concrete: disclose the whole cost picture in one breath, meaning the build fee, what recurs monthly, what is billed separately and how a change order is priced; never sell on manufactured fear, which covers invented hacking threats, invented search penalties and invented deadlines; never run a pressure close on someone who has said they want to think or to consult a partner; and take deliberate extra care with buyers who cannot evaluate the technical claims being made to them, such as an older owner buying their first site, someone working in a second language, or someone who has just been burned and will agree to anything. With those buyers the operator slows down, puts the offer in plain writing, invites a second reader, and treats a signature obtained through confusion as worthless. Any fee-sharing with a referral partner is disclosed to the client rather than buried inside the price.

included: disclosure-first pricing conversation
the ban on fear-selling, invented urgency and pressure closes
extra care for buyers who cannot evaluate the claims
disclosure of partner fee-sharing
excluded: jurisdiction-specific contract and consumer-protection rules, which the operator verifies locally

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client reports being surprised by a cost or a term, or a jurisdictional rule on selling practice or commercial contact changes

pros.claim: Conduct that reads well when repeated is the cheapest referral insurance available in a niche where everyone talks
pros.example: an owner telling their trade group that the quote included the monthly fee up front and that nothing was added afterwards

cons.claim: Disclosure-first loses deals that a vaguer competitor closes on the build fee alone
cons.example: a prospect choosing a cheaper-looking quote that never mentioned a monthly cost until after launch

failure_modes: burying the recurring fee in a footnote so the first monthly invoice arrives as a surprise
using a security scare or a search-penalty story to move an undecided buyer
taking a signature from a buyer who cannot restate what they have agreed to
paying or accepting a referral fee that the client is never told about
acceptance_tests: the recurring cost is stated aloud and in writing before any signature is requested
no proposal or outreach script contains a threat, an invented deadline or an unverifiable risk claim
any partner fee-sharing arrangement is stated to the client in plain language
revisit_triggers: a client is surprised by a charge they were told about, which means the disclosure is not landing
a partner arrangement changes how money moves between the parties

nodes.definition: Write the literal list of what a buyer receives for the build fee, in the buyer's language and with the edges included: how many pages and which ones, that the design comes from the operator's repeatable layout rather than a blank canvas, what happens to supplied content versus what the client must write, how many review rounds are included and what a round actually means, and what is set up at launch such as form delivery to an address the client controls and basic analytics. The half that prevents most disputes is the explicit not-included list: online store, bookings and payments, logo design, photography, copywriting beyond light editing, third-party integrations and ongoing marketing. Each request that recurs in this niche gets a named add-on so it can be priced from the same cost floor instead of argued about mid-build.

included: the page and feature line items
the definition of a review round
the explicit not-included list
the named add-on menu
excluded: how the pages are built and with which tools
the price of each line item

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recurring out-of-list requests or a dispute show the inventory no longer matches what the niche buys

pros.claim: A written not-included list turns the most common mid-build argument into a two-minute reference to a document both parties signed
pros.example: pointing at the not-included line for online payments when a florist asks mid-build to start taking orders on the site

cons.claim: An explicit inventory can read as mean-spirited to a buyer who expected a partner rather than a product
cons.example: a first-time buyer reading a page of exclusions and feeling counted against before any work has started

failure_modes: listing only what is included and leaving the boundary to be discovered during the build
writing the list in production jargon the buyer cannot check against their own expectations
letting the list drift silently as favours accumulate until nobody can say what the standard build is
acceptance_tests: every line item states what the client gets and who supplies its input
the not-included list names the requests that actually recur in this niche, each paired with an add-on or a decline
revisit_triggers: the same out-of-list request appears on several consecutive deals
a dispute traces back to something the inventory never mentioned

nodes.definition: Define what the monthly fee buys in the honest form the client will hold the operator to a year later: custody of a working site, meaning hosting and domain administration, backups that are taken and proven restorable, platform and plugin updates, security and uptime checking, and a bounded allowance of small edits with a stated response window, plus the matching list of what is not in it such as redesigns, new pages beyond the allowance, marketing campaigns and third-party subscriptions the client owns directly. Tiers exist only where they correspond to a real difference in work or resource, and unlimited edits is refused as a promise because it prices an unknown; the allowance is stated as a bounded budget with a definition of what counts as small and a named overflow path. This node fixes the promise at the moment of sale, while how the work is actually operated month to month belongs to the hosting-care-plan-and-retention KB.

included: the promise set of the monthly leg as stated at sale
tier differences that correspond to real work or resource
the bounded edit allowance and its overflow path
the not-included list for the recurring leg
excluded: backup, patching, security and monitoring operations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured monthly work per site or repeated client requests show the promise set no longer matches what the plan really does

pros.claim: A bounded allowance with a named overflow path makes 'edits included' a promise both sides can check
pros.example: a client asking for a fourth change in a month and being quoted the overflow basis printed on the sheet they signed, with nobody feeling cheated

cons.claim: Bounded promises look weaker on paper than a competitor's unlimited support until the client has lived through both
cons.example: losing a side-by-side comparison to a plan advertising unlimited edits that quietly stretches its response times instead

failure_modes: promising unlimited anything and pricing an unknown into a monthly fee
listing tiers that differ only in price, so the client cannot see what the extra money buys
describing the plan in operator terms such as patching and monitoring that the buyer cannot value
acceptance_tests: each tier names at least one concrete difference in included work or resource rather than only a price
the edit allowance states its size, what counts as a small edit and what happens when it is exceeded
revisit_triggers: measured support time per site drifts away from the allowance the plan promises
clients repeatedly ask for something the plan neither includes nor names

nodes.definition: Derive the build fee from the operator's own numbers instead of from a price remembered off someone else's website. The mechanism has four inputs: the hours the standard package actually takes end to end on recent builds, including content chasing, review rounds and launch, valued at the rate the operator needs their working hours to earn; the third-party costs that pass through a build such as a domain year, theme or plugin licences, stock imagery and email setup; a rework reserve sized from how often builds have needed unpaid extra rounds; and the share of unbilled selling and admin time that each closed deal has to carry. The sum is a floor rather than a price, because quoting below it means paying to work, and the only honest ways to move it are to reduce the hours through repetition or to change what is in the package. It is re-derived from the operator's own time record as build times change, and every quote is checked against it deal by deal.

included: the cost-floor mechanism and its four inputs
re-derivation from the operator's own time and cost record
the rule that every quote is checked against the floor
excluded: stating any market rate or typical price as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the time record shows build hours or pass-through costs moving away from the figures the floor was built on

pros.claim: A floor derived from measured hours turns pricing from a nerve test into arithmetic the operator can defend calmly
pros.example: knowing the measured span of hours the last several five-page builds consumed and quoting from that rather than from a competitor's advertised figure

cons.claim: The floor is only as honest as the time record behind it, and solo operators systematically under-record their own hours
cons.example: a build that felt like two days but consumed a week of evenings chasing photographs, none of which was ever logged

failure_modes: setting the fee by copying an advertised price from another web shop and calling it market research
leaving content chasing, review rounds and admin outside the measured hours
never re-deriving the floor after the package or the build time has changed
acceptance_tests: the floor can be reconstructed from a written list of hours, pass-through costs, rework reserve and overhead share
the most recent quotes can each be shown to sit above the floor or to carry a disclosed reason why they do not
revisit_triggers: measured build hours move materially in either direction
a pass-through cost such as a licence or a domain renewal changes

nodes.definition: Build the monthly price the same way as the build fee: from the cost of keeping one site alive for a month across the operator's whole portfolio, never from what other providers advertise. The inputs are the per-site share of infrastructure, meaning the hosting capacity divided across the sites it holds plus backup storage and the monitoring, security and update tooling amortised over every site under management; the labour reserve for the promised work, meaning the measured minutes of updates, checks and small edits a typical site consumes in a month plus the occasional month when something breaks; an incident reserve for the support call that cannot wait; and the margin that makes operating the recurring leg worth doing at all. Tier steps come from real step-changes in that cost, such as more resource, more included edit time or a faster response window. The whole derivation is re-checked against the actual per-site cost ledger on a regular cadence, because a plan priced on last year's portfolio and tooling quietly stops covering itself.

included: the per-site cost inputs and the labour and incident reserves
tier steps tied to real cost or work differences
the periodic re-derivation against the cost ledger
excluded: quoting any market monthly figure as fact
how backups, patching and monitoring are actually operated

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the per-site cost ledger or the measured monthly support minutes move away from the figures the price was derived from

pros.claim: Pricing from a per-site cost ledger means a growing portfolio makes the recurring leg stronger rather than quietly more fragile
pros.example: noticing that backup storage and monitoring cost per site fell as the portfolio grew and choosing to widen the edit allowance instead of cutting the price

cons.claim: Per-site costs are lumpy and shared, so the allocation is always an estimate that can be argued with
cons.example: one heavy site consuming most of a shared hosting plan's resources while paying the same as five quiet ones

failure_modes: pricing the monthly fee to match a competitor's advertised number and discovering the labour reserve was never inside it
forgetting that the promised edit allowance is paid labour rather than a rounding error
never re-deriving after the portfolio, the tooling or the hosting bill has changed
acceptance_tests: the monthly price can be traced to per-site infrastructure share, labour reserve, incident reserve and margin
each tier step names the cost or work difference that justifies it
revisit_triggers: hosting, backup or tooling costs change
measured support minutes per site drift beyond the labour reserve

nodes.definition: Decide how much of the total client value sits in the one-time fee and how much in the monthly one, and understand what each split does to the business. A full build fee with a modest plan pays the operator now, survives churn well and suits a buyer who dislikes subscriptions, but every month starts from zero. A subsidised build with a stronger plan lowers the entry barrier and builds the annuity, but it lends the client money: the unrecovered build cost has to be earned back over months of retention, so an early cancellation is a loss and a churn rate the operator has never measured becomes the largest hidden risk in the model. The reasoning is per-client payback, meaning how many months of the plan it takes to recover what the build actually cost, what happens if the client leaves before then, and whether the deposit and the terms make that outcome survivable without inventing an exit penalty.

included: the split decision and its cashflow consequences
per-client payback reasoning in plan-months
early-cancellation exposure and how it is absorbed

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed client life in the first cohorts replaces the assumed retention the split was chosen on

pros.claim: Thinking in payback months makes the difference between a discount and a loan visible before it is granted
pros.example: seeing that a heavily subsidised build only breaks even after many months of the plan and requiring a deposit that at least covers the pass-through costs

cons.claim: Payback reasoning rests on a retention assumption a new operator has no evidence for yet
cons.example: modelling the annuity on a multi-year client life when the first cohort has existed for only a few months

failure_modes: subsidising builds to win deals without ever measuring how long clients actually stay
treating recurring revenue as profit while unrecovered build cost is still outstanding
using the plan price as the discount lever, which degrades the promise every existing client is already paying for
acceptance_tests: for the standard package the payback in plan-months is written down and refreshed whenever either price moves
the cancellation term states what happens to unamortised build cost and the client was told before signing
revisit_triggers: a cohort of clients cancels earlier than the payback assumption
either derived price changes materially

nodes.definition: Settle the commercial terms that travel with every deal and say them before the signature: the deposit that starts work and what it covers, when the balance falls due against a milestone that is not 'when the client feels finished', when the first monthly charge begins and how it is collected, the notice period for cancelling the plan and what the client keeps when they do, how and with how much warning a price may change, and what a stalled project costs when the client goes quiet. These terms are the practical expression of the ownership pledge and the disclosure rule, so they must be readable by a non-technical owner in a couple of minutes, must contain no clause whose real purpose is to make leaving expensive, and must name the obligation classes involved, including written-contract, cancellation-rights, consumer-protection and recurring-billing rules, which the operator verifies in their own jurisdiction rather than assuming.

included: deposit, balance milestone and billing start
cancellation notice and what the client keeps
price-change notice and stall terms
the obligation classes to verify locally
excluded: drafting legal language or giving legal advice
offboarding execution and asset handover mechanics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a local rule on contracts, cancellation or recurring billing changes, or a dispute exposes an undefined term

pros.claim: Terms a non-technical owner can read in two minutes close faster than terms that need explaining
pros.example: a one-page sheet where the deposit, the monthly start date and the cancellation notice each occupy a single line

cons.claim: Simple client-favourable terms give away leverage a harsher contract would keep
cons.example: a short cancellation notice with no exit fee letting a client who never really engaged leave immediately after launch

failure_modes: starting a build on a verbal agreement where the deposit was never defined
burying the monthly start date so the first charge arrives as a surprise
copying contract clauses from another jurisdiction and assuming they hold in this one
adding an exit fee whose real function is to prevent leaving rather than to recover a cost
acceptance_tests: deposit, balance milestone, plan start, cancellation notice and price-change notice each appear as one plain sentence in the signed document
no clause exists whose only effect is to raise the cost of leaving
revisit_triggers: a jurisdictional rule on contracts, cancellation rights or recurring billing changes
a payment dispute exposes a term nobody had written down

nodes.definition: Assemble the evidence a stranger needs in order to believe a solo operator can deliver, and assemble it honestly. Before there are clients that means work which is real but plainly labelled: a site built for a business the operator already knows, a demonstration build for the target trade marked as a demonstration, or a rebuild of a visibly broken public page presented as an unsolicited example rather than as client work. After the first deliveries it means permission-based case studies, meaning the client's name used with consent, before-and-after screenshots, measured facts the client would confirm, and a testimonial in the client's own words. Nothing is invented: no borrowed logos, no fabricated testimonials, no stock clients and no outcome attributed to the site that the named client would not repeat. The operator's own website and local listings are part of the proof set, because a web shop whose own site is slow or stale contradicts every claim it makes.

included: labelled demonstration work before there are clients
permission-based case studies and testimonials
the operator's own site and listings as part of the proof
excluded: fabricated or borrowed credentials of any kind
outcome claims that cannot be verified

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a permission is withdrawn, a portfolio item ages out of the current package, or a claim inside the proof set is found unverifiable

pros.claim: One well-documented before-and-after in the target trade outperforms a page of adjectives
pros.example: a screenshot pair showing a roofer's unreadable phone page beside the rebuilt one, published with that client's permission

cons.claim: Honest proof accumulates slowly, so the earliest months are spent selling with very little of it
cons.example: a first outreach cycle carrying one labelled demonstration site and no client names at all

failure_modes: dressing a demonstration build up as a real client engagement
publishing a client's site or name in a portfolio without asking them
claiming a business outcome the client never attributed to the site
letting the operator's own site rot while selling site quality to others
acceptance_tests: every portfolio item is either a real engagement shown with permission or is visibly labelled as a demonstration
every stated result is one the named client would confirm if asked
revisit_triggers: a client asks for their work to be removed from the portfolio
the strongest case study drifts out of date relative to the current package

nodes.definition: Reach the businesses in the niche that show an observable, checkable problem, such as no site at all, a site that fails on a phone, a dead or expired page, or a listing whose phone number no longer works, and open with that specific observation rather than with a pitch or a scare. The channels that work for local owners are the ones that respect how they work: a short visit in the quiet part of their day, a call at a time their trade is not on site, a brief message naming the specific page and the specific problem with an offer to fix it, and follow-up that stops the moment the answer is no. The observation must be true and re-checkable by the owner, the message must say who is writing and why, and before running any volume the operator verifies the jurisdiction's rules on unsolicited commercial calls, messages and email, which is an obligation class rather than a detail.

included: choosing prospects on an observable defect
channel choice suited to how local owners work
the specific-observation opening and the stop-on-no rule
excluded: bought lists and automated bulk mailing
the jurisdiction's specific commercial-contact rules, which the operator verifies locally

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recorded response rates by channel change, or a commercial-contact rule or platform policy is updated

pros.claim: Opening with a defect the owner can see on their own phone converts far better than any description of services
pros.example: showing a plumber standing at their own counter that the number on their site cannot be tapped to dial

cons.claim: Manual, respectful outreach is slow and mostly declined, which is hard to sustain alone
cons.example: a week of visits and calls producing one scoping conversation and a lot of polite refusals

failure_modes: turning the observation into a threat about hacking or search penalties
continuing to follow up after a clear no
running message volume without first checking the local commercial-contact rules
leading with price before the owner has agreed there is a problem worth fixing
acceptance_tests: every opening message names a specific, currently true, client-checkable observation
a contacted-and-declined list exists and is honoured on the next cycle
revisit_triggers: response rate collapses on a channel
a rule or platform policy governing commercial contact changes

nodes.definition: Build the loop that makes acquisition cheaper every year: a delivered site, an owner who is visibly pleased at an identifiable moment, an ask that is easy to say yes to, and a record of where every client came from. The moments that work are narrow, being launch day when the owner first shows the site to someone, the first inquiry that arrives through the form, and the first month of the care plan when a small edit was handled quickly. The ask has to be small and concrete, such as one name, one introduction or a forwarded sentence the owner can send as it is written, rather than a vague request to spread the word. Reciprocity matters, so the operator sends work back to clients and partners wherever it fits. Every closed deal records its source, because that record is what distinguishes a channel that is actually feeding the business from one that merely feels productive.

included: the referral moments and the small concrete ask
making the introduction easy to pass on
source tracking on every closed deal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the recorded share of deals arriving by referral moves up or down across a full quarter

pros.claim: A referred prospect arrives already trusting the operator, which shortens the sale and reduces price shopping
pros.example: a landscaper's introduction to a fellow contractor closing in one conversation with no competing quotes sought

cons.claim: The loop starts slowly and produces nothing at all until the first deliveries are genuinely good
cons.example: a first quarter with no referrals because only two sites exist and neither owner has had a reason to mention them

failure_modes: asking for a referral at a moment of friction rather than at a moment of visible satisfaction
asking so vaguely that the owner cannot act on it
never recording deal sources and over-investing in a channel that produced nothing
offering a referral reward that the introduced client is never told about
acceptance_tests: each delivered project has a recorded referral ask made at a named moment
every client record names the source that produced it
revisit_triggers: the referral share of new deals falls across a quarter
a niche network goes quiet after a delivery that went badly

nodes.definition: Cultivate the small set of local providers who touch the same owner around the same decision: sign-writers and print shops doing a rebrand, photographers shooting premises and staff, bookkeepers who see every business bill, information-technology and point-of-sale installers, marketing freelancers who want a site built but not maintained, and the trade associations or chambers where the niche gathers. A partner channel is only worth having when the partner's own reputation is on the line each time they introduce someone, which means the operator's delivery has to be good enough that the introduction is safe to make. Arrangements stay simple and disclosed, being either reciprocal introductions or a fee the client is told about; an undisclosed payment is never taken or paid, and no arrangement is allowed to push a client toward something they do not need.

included: identifying the adjacent providers who share the buyer
reciprocity as the default arrangement
disclosure of any fee-sharing to the client
excluded: white-label or reseller agreements with hosting vendors, which the care-plan KB owns
the delivery quality that makes an introduction safe to give

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a partner relationship starts, stops or changes the money that moves through it

pros.claim: A partner introduces the buyer at exactly the moment the need appears, which no cold channel can time
pros.example: a sign-writer mentioning the operator while quoting new van livery for a business whose website still shows the old branding

cons.claim: Partner channels are few, slow to build and can vanish with a single bad handoff
cons.example: a photographer stopping introductions after one referred client complained about a missed deadline

failure_modes: treating partners as a lead list rather than a relationship with reciprocity
accepting a fee arrangement the end client is never told about
letting a partner promise things about the site that the operator has not agreed to deliver
acceptance_tests: each active partner arrangement is written in one paragraph including any money that changes hands and how the client is told
every partner-introduced client is traceable to its partner in the source record
revisit_triggers: a partner's introductions stop, or a partner-referred project ends badly
a partner starts describing the offer inaccurately to prospects

nodes.definition: Impose a rhythm that survives delivery weeks, because the characteristic way this business dies is feast and famine: the operator sells three builds, disappears into them for a month, launches, and finds an empty pipeline and no income for the following six weeks. The cadence has four parts: a small non-negotiable weekly allocation of prospecting and follow-up that happens even in the busiest build week, a simple written record of every live conversation with its next action and date, a reading of which channel produced each closed deal, and a capacity limit stating how many concurrent builds one operator can carry before review rounds and care-plan work start slipping. That limit is what turns selling a fourth build in a month from a win into a scheduling decision that has to be made deliberately.

included: the protected weekly prospecting allocation
the live-conversation record with next actions
the concurrent-build capacity limit
per-channel yield reading
excluded: the content of any outreach message

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the pipeline record shows a delivery month with no started conversations or a breach of the capacity limit

pros.claim: A protected weekly slot removes the income gap that follows every busy delivery month
pros.example: two hours of follow-up held every Tuesday morning even during a launch week, so the next scoping call is booked before the current build ends

cons.claim: Protecting selling time during delivery pushes launch dates out and can irritate the client currently being served
cons.example: a review round answered a day later because the prospecting block was not moved

failure_modes: treating prospecting as what happens when there is nothing else to do
keeping the pipeline in memory rather than in a record, so follow-ups are missed
selling past the capacity limit and degrading the delivery quality that produces referrals
acceptance_tests: a written pipeline record shows every live conversation with a next action and a date
the weekly prospecting allocation was honoured during the most recent busy delivery week
revisit_triggers: a delivery month passed with no new conversations started
concurrent builds exceeded the stated capacity limit

nodes.definition: Run the one structured conversation that decides whether a prospect becomes a deal, and run it the same way every time: what the business does and who its customers are, what the owner wants the site to do in their own words, who will supply the text and photographs and by when, who currently owns the domain and where the business email lives, what exists today that must be preserved, when they need to be live and why that date exists, who else has to approve, and roughly what they expected to spend. The second half of the conversation is disqualification, which is a skill rather than a failure: an online store or booking system beyond the package, a committee of decision-makers, a fixed launch date depending on content nobody will write, an expectation of ranking or lead guarantees that has already been refused, a budget below the cost floor with no willingness to reduce scope, or an owner who describes every previous vendor as a villain. Walking away early is cheaper than any of the alternatives.

included: the standard intake question set
recording domain, host and email custody exactly as found
the disqualification signals and the decline as a normal outcome
excluded: changing anything about the client's domain, DNS or email, which the delivery KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a delivered project fails for a cause the standard intake never asked about

pros.claim: A repeated question set surfaces the deal-killers in twenty minutes instead of three weeks into a build
pros.example: learning on the first call that a restaurant's photographs belong to a photographer who has not been paid, before any launch date is discussed

cons.claim: A rigid script can feel like an interrogation to an owner who wanted a conversation
cons.example: a sole trader who wanted to talk about their business hearing a checklist and disengaging

failure_modes: quoting before knowing who supplies the content
skipping the domain and email custody questions and discovering at launch that nobody can reach the registrar
accepting a deal that showed a known disqualifying signal because the pipeline was thin
letting the prospect's urgency set a launch date the content cannot possibly meet
acceptance_tests: every intake records content ownership and dates, domain and email custody as they stand today, the decision-maker, and the live job the site must do
at least one disqualification signal is checked explicitly and its answer recorded
revisit_triggers: a project goes wrong for a reason the intake never asked about
a change to the package alters what a good-fit prospect looks like

nodes.definition: Assign in writing, before the build starts, the single most common reason small-business web projects stall, which is the content. That means naming who writes each page's text, who supplies photographs and whether they are licensed for use, who provides a usable version of the logo, who confirms opening hours and service areas are accurate, and the date each of those arrives. It also means pricing the honest alternatives, so light editing of what the client sends stays inside the package, writing the pages for them is a priced add-on, and a photo shoot is somebody else's trade. Finally it sets the stall rule: what happens when content does not arrive, which is that the project parks at a named point, the launch date moves by the delay, and the deposit does not fund an indefinite hold. Filler text written to fill a gap never goes live, and keeping it is never the operator's decision to make alone.

included: per-page content ownership and dates
image licensing responsibility
copywriting as a priced add-on
the stall and park rule
excluded: the content intake mechanics of the build pipeline
where assets are stored and hosted

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: content lateness recurs across projects or an image-licensing problem surfaces

pros.claim: A named owner and a date per page turn the vaguest part of the project into something either done or visibly late
pros.example: a checklist showing that the about-page text and three photographs are outstanding, dated, and blocking the launch week

cons.claim: Making content the client's job puts the schedule in the hands of the person least able to protect it
cons.example: a builder who fully intends to write their services page and is then on a roof for three weeks

failure_modes: starting a build on the promise that content is coming
letting filler text written to fill a gap drift toward launch day
publishing client-supplied images with no idea who owns the rights
absorbing the writing for free and teaching the client that words are included
acceptance_tests: every page has a named content owner and a date recorded before the build starts
the stall rule and its effect on the launch date appear in the signed scope
revisit_triggers: content arrives late on consecutive projects, meaning the rule is unenforced or the dates are unrealistic
a client supplies imagery with unclear licensing

nodes.definition: Produce the one document that is simultaneously the proposal and the operative half of the contract, written so a busy owner reads it in a few minutes: the live job the site must do in their words, the deliverable inventory with its not-included list, the named content owners and dates, the review-round rules, the build fee and what the deposit starts, the monthly plan with its allowance and start date, the ownership pledge, the change-order mechanism and the basis on which extras are priced, and a launch date expressed as conditional on the content arriving. Nothing verbal survives outside it. The signature is requested only after the recurring cost has been stated aloud, and the copy the client keeps is the reference both sides return to for every later 'I thought that was included'.

included: the single proposal-and-scope document and its required sections
conditional launch dating
the change-order mechanism and its price basis
the signature-after-disclosure rule
excluded: legal drafting and jurisdiction-specific contract wording

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute or a change to the package, prices or terms shows a section of the document is missing or wrong

pros.claim: One signed page ends nearly every later dispute because both parties are reading the same sentence
pros.example: settling a disagreement about a fourth review round by reading the two-included-rounds line together

cons.claim: Producing a real scope document per deal is unpaid work done before any money has arrived
cons.example: an evening spent scoping a prospect who then chooses a cheaper quote that came with no document at all

failure_modes: agreeing scope in a phone call and confirming none of it in writing
quoting a fixed launch date that does not depend on the content dates
leaving the change-order price basis undefined so every extra becomes a fresh negotiation
asking for the signature before the monthly fee has been stated plainly
acceptance_tests: the signed document contains the job, the inventory, the exclusions, the content owners and dates, both prices, the plan start, the ownership pledge and the change mechanism
the client holds their own copy and can point to the line that answers a scope question
revisit_triggers: a dispute traces to something the document did not cover
the package, either price mechanism or the terms change

nodes.definition: Spend the ten minutes after signing that save the project by telling the client how the work will actually feel: which channel to send things to and what response time to expect, that feedback comes back consolidated once per round from one named decision-maker rather than as a stream of messages from three people, what a review round is and what happens once the included ones are used, what launch day looks like and what remains adjustable afterwards, what the first month of the care plan includes and how to ask for an edit. The part most operators skip is the last one: restating what the site will and will not do for the business in the same honest terms used during the sale, so the client's private hope of a ranking miracle is retired before launch rather than after it.

included: communication channel and response-window expectations
the consolidated-feedback and single-decision-maker rule
the launch-day and first-care-month picture
restating the honest outcome limits after signing
excluded: the build's internal steps and technical checkpoints

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: review rounds or client communication repeatedly break the rules the briefing was supposed to set

pros.claim: Expectations set before the first review round decide whether a client feels served or ignored, at no cost
pros.example: a client who knows that a Saturday message is answered on Monday and therefore does not read the silence as neglect

cons.claim: A briefing full of rules can feel bureaucratic to an owner who wanted an informal relationship
cons.example: a sole trader who prefers texting at odd hours being asked to use one channel and one consolidated round of feedback

failure_modes: assuming a signed scope has already set the working rules
letting feedback arrive from several people with no named decision-maker
leaving the ranking expectation unaddressed because the client seemed satisfied at signing
promising a response speed the operator cannot hold during a build week
acceptance_tests: the client can state the channel, the response window, the number of review rounds and what happens at launch
the honest outcome limits were restated after signing rather than only during the sale
revisit_triggers: feedback arrives outside the agreed channel or from unnamed people on consecutive projects
a client voices an outcome expectation the briefing was supposed to have retired

nodes.definition: Handle the steady pressure of small out-of-scope requests in a way that protects both the margin and the relationship, because refusing everything costs referrals while absorbing everything converts a fixed-price build into unpaid hourly work. The method has three parts. Recognise the patterns early: the 'while you are in there' request, an extra page arriving as an afterthought, a third review round framed as a correction, a social-media or email problem that is not the site at all, and a family member's opinion arriving late. Keep a small explicit goodwill allowance the operator is willing to spend without ceremony and can state out loud. Route anything past it through the change-order mechanism the scope already defines, named, priced and dated before the work happens, even when the answer is no charge but the launch moves. The most dangerous creep is the free favour that becomes precedent, because a small edit done silently during the build teaches the client exactly what they think the care plan includes.

included: the recognition patterns for creep
a bounded, stateable goodwill allowance
routing extras through change orders
the precedent rule
excluded: the care plan's operational edit workflow

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recorded change orders and goodwill spend show one request recurring or the allowance being overrun

pros.claim: A named goodwill allowance lets the operator be generous on purpose rather than resentfully by accident
pros.example: adding a staff photograph at no charge and saying plainly that it comes out of the goodwill allowance, so the next request is understood as chargeable

cons.claim: Change orders for small items can make the operator look rigid beside a competitor who says yes to everything
cons.example: a client comparing a change-order note for a fifth page with a friend's developer who simply adds pages

failure_modes: absorbing extras silently and resetting the client's baseline expectation
pricing a trivial favour and damaging the relationship that produces referrals
allowing a third review round because refusing felt awkward in the moment
adding scope without recording that the launch date moved with it
acceptance_tests: every out-of-scope item is either inside the stated goodwill allowance or carries a written change order agreed before the work happens
the goodwill allowance has a size the operator can state out loud
revisit_triggers: the same extra is requested on most projects, which means it belongs in the package or the add-on menu
goodwill work consistently overruns its allowance

nodes.definition: Gate the moment where selling stops and building begins, so the delivery process inherits a complete package instead of a promise. The handoff carries the signed scope with its inventory and exclusions, the deposit received, the content inventory with each item marked supplied or outstanding with its date, the recorded facts about the domain registrar, the current host and where business email lives, recorded exactly as found and changed by nobody at this stage, the client's named decision-maker and channel, the launch-date condition, the care-plan start date and tier, and any change orders already agreed. If an item is missing the build does not start: the project sits in a named waiting state with the specific missing item visible to the client. This gate is the anti-rework rule of the whole subdomain, because everything discovered here costs minutes and the same thing discovered after the build starts costs days and a moved launch.

included: the handoff checklist contents
the do-not-start rule and the named waiting state
recording domain, host and email custody facts exactly as found
excluded: performing any DNS, hosting or email change, which the delivery KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a build stalls on a missing input the checklist never asked for, or the delivery process changes its intake requirements

pros.claim: A hard gate turns the classic mid-build discovery into a pre-build question that costs minutes
pros.example: finding at handoff that the domain sits in a former employee's personal account, before any launch date has been promised to the client's customers

cons.claim: Holding a paid deal in a waiting state frustrates a client who feels they have already bought
cons.example: a client who paid the deposit on Friday and cannot understand why the build is waiting on three photographs

failure_modes: starting the build while content is described as nearly ready
handing over a scope that cannot be executed because no decision-maker was ever named
changing DNS or email settings during the sales stage to be helpful and breaking a working business mailbox
leaving the care-plan start date unset so the recurring leg begins late or never begins at all
acceptance_tests: no build starts until every checklist item is either supplied or explicitly waived in writing
the handoff package names the domain, host and email custody facts as they were found
revisit_triggers: a build stalls on something the handoff checklist did not capture
the delivery process changes what it needs from the sale

edges.why_related: the line-item inventory is the concrete expression of the decision to sell a package rather than hours
the claims line is drawn against the jobs buyers actually hire a site for, which makes each refusal specific instead of abstract
the recurring promise is written against what was actually built, so the plan cannot promise custody of something the package never delivered
there is nothing to cost until the deliverable list is fixed, because the measured hours are hours spent on named line items
the monthly price is derived from the work the plan promises, so the promise set has to exist before the labour reserve can be sized
the split can only be reasoned about once the true cost of the build leg is known
payback in plan-months is computed from the monthly figure and the margin inside it
the deposit, billing and cancellation terms are the instrument that makes the chosen split survivable
cold outreach needs something real to show the moment a prospect asks what the operator has done before
a permitted case study is what makes an introduction easy for a client to pass on without having to explain anything
the intake conversation only happens if the cadence keeps producing conversations to have
the scope document is written from what the intake recorded, so an incomplete intake produces an unwritable scope
the content owners, dates and stall rule are required sections of the signed document
the deposit, plan start, cancellation and price-change lines live inside the same document the client signs
the signed scope is the first item on the handoff checklist and the reference the builder works from
portfolio and case-study claims are bound by the same verifiability rule as sales claims, so a case study may only state what the named client would confirm
the post-signature briefing must restate the same refusals, so nothing softens in the gap between the sale and the build
no term may turn assets the client owns into leverage, which rules out exit fees and withheld access on cancellation
the plan may administer the client's domain, files and inbox but may never be the only route to them
the opening observation must be true and checkable and follow-up stops at no, which excludes fear scripts and invented deadlines
any money moving between the operator and a partner is disclosed to the client, which rules out silent commissions
a real prospect's needs rarely match the standard package exactly, and the easiest path to a signature is to let the package quietly bend
edges.resolution_rule: the package bends only through a named add-on priced from the same cost floor, otherwise the prospect is declined; when the same misfit appears on several consecutive deals it is redesigned into the package deliberately rather than improvised deal by deal

edges.why_related: a thin pipeline creates pressure to discount below the derived floor in order to convert the prospect who is actually in front of you
edges.resolution_rule: reduce scope rather than price; a below-floor number is only offered as an openly disclosed, time-bounded founding-client arrangement that buys a reference, still covers pass-through cost, and is never funded by thinning the care plan the client will receive

edges.why_related: the claim that would convert fastest, a promise about rankings or lead volume, is exactly the claim the business refuses to make
edges.resolution_rule: the refusal holds without exception; the conversion gap is closed with a checkable observation and a measured before-and-after on the client's own site, and a prospect who will only buy a guarantee is recorded as a decline

edges.why_related: client-held ownership removes the switching cost that would otherwise protect the payback on a subsidised build
edges.resolution_rule: ownership is never traded for retention; the payback is protected by a deposit that covers pass-through cost, an honest split and service quality, never by making departure difficult or expensive

edges.why_related: the generosity that earns enthusiastic introductions is the same behaviour that erodes a fixed-price margin
edges.resolution_rule: generosity is spent from a stated goodwill allowance and named as such when given; beyond the allowance a change order is written even at zero price, so the client experiences the generosity without learning that scope is free

edges.why_related: a narrow niche makes the offer repeatable but empties the local pool, while taking whatever arrives fills the calendar and destroys repeatability
edges.resolution_rule: hold the niche for the standard package and its assets; out-of-niche work is accepted only when it fits the package unchanged and is priced from the same floor, and the niche decision is re-read on recorded conversion rather than on the mood of a slow month

edges.why_related: the client wants a firm launch date while the schedule depends on content that only they can supply
edges.resolution_rule: the launch date is always stated as conditional on the content dates; when content slips the date moves by the same amount and the project parks at the named point rather than the operator silently writing the client's pages unpaid

edges.why_related: owners in one trade know each other through suppliers, associations and job sites, so niche density is what makes the referral loop compound instead of trickle
the client who introduces peers is the one whose experience matched what they were told, so met expectations rather than heroics produce referrals
what the plan promises determines the labour reserve, which determines how much of the recurring revenue is actually margin available to fund a subsidised build
content readiness is the input that most often decides whether a signed deal can enter the build at all or sits in the waiting state
the pledge exists before intake so the discovery conversation can record who holds the domain and email today and tell the client what they will own tomorrow
a partner is asked to stake their own reputation only after there is work that can be shown to the person they introduce
an extra requested on most projects is evidence that the package or the add-on menu is wrong, not that clients are being unreasonable
recorded per-channel and per-trade conversion is the evidence that reopens the niche decision instead of leaving it to impression
measured support minutes and observed cancellation timing feed back into the per-site labour reserve and the tier steps
both prices are derived the same way, from the operator's own measured cost ledger plus a reserve and a margin, so the discipline learned on one transfers directly to the other

conflict_axes.name: package_discipline_vs_deal_fit
conflict_axes.description: Every real prospect wants something slightly outside the standard build, and the shortest path to a signature is to let the package quietly bend.
poles: fit the deal in front of you
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bend only through a priced add-on or an honest decline, and treat a repeated misfit as evidence to redesign the package deliberately

conflict_axes.name: cost_floor_vs_closing_the_deal
conflict_axes.description: A derived floor says no to a price that a slow month says yes to.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reduce scope rather than price; below-floor numbers only as a disclosed, time-bounded founding arrangement that buys a reference and still covers pass-through cost

conflict_axes.name: recurring_annuity_vs_upfront_cash
conflict_axes.description: Subsidising the build grows the annuity but lends the client money, while taking the fee up front pays now and starts every month from zero.
poles: subsidise the build to grow the annuity
take the full fee up front
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose the split on payback months and measured retention, and while retention is still unmeasured keep the deposit covering pass-through cost

conflict_axes.name: honest_limits_vs_persuasive_promises
conflict_axes.description: The promise that converts fastest, about rankings or lead volume, is the one that cannot be verified or kept.
poles: claim only what can be measured
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verifiability is absolute; replace the missing promise with a checkable observation and a measured before-and-after, and let guarantee-seeking prospects go

conflict_axes.name: client_ownership_vs_switching_cost
conflict_axes.description: Everything that makes a client free to leave also removes the friction that would have kept a wobbling account.
poles: the client owns everything and can leave
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ownership is not negotiable; retention is earned by service quality and the documented exit path is shown on request

conflict_axes.name: niche_repeatability_vs_market_size
conflict_axes.description: Staying narrow makes every build cheaper and every referral warmer, while widening keeps the calendar full and the assets generic.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the niche for the package and its assets, accept out-of-niche work only unchanged and at the same floor, and re-read the decision on recorded conversion

conflict_axes.name: goodwill_generosity_vs_margin_protection
conflict_axes.description: The small free favour that earns a referral is the same act that teaches the client scope is free.
poles: charge for everything out of scope
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spend a stated goodwill allowance visibly and write a change order beyond it even at zero price, so generosity never becomes precedent

conflict_axes.name: firm_launch_date_vs_client_supplied_content
conflict_axes.description: The client wants a date they can announce while the schedule depends on words and photographs only they can produce.
poles: protect the schedule from content risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make dates conditional on content dates, move the date by the slippage and park the project rather than becoming an unpaid copywriter

conflict_axes.name: selling_time_vs_delivery_time
conflict_axes.description: The hours that keep the pipeline alive are taken from the client currently being served, and the hours that delight that client are taken from the pipeline.
poles: serve the client in front of you
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the smallest prospecting allocation that survives a launch week and cap concurrent builds so neither leg starves the other

conflict_axes.name: unbounded_sounding_plan_vs_honest_allowance
conflict_axes.description: An unlimited-sounding care plan sells better on a comparison sheet than a bounded one that can actually be delivered.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: refuse unlimited, state the allowance and what counts as a small edit, name the overflow path, and then out-deliver inside the stated bound

edge_cases.description: A prospect will sign today if given a first-page-of-search guarantee
edge_cases.trigger: a buyer makes an outcome guarantee the condition of the deal
edge_cases.mitigation: restate what will be measured and shown instead, offer the checkable before-and-after on their own pages, and let the deal go if the guarantee is the condition, recording it as a disqualification reason

edge_cases.description: The client's domain is registered inside a former developer's personal account and nobody can reach him
edge_cases.trigger: intake finds the domain held by an unreachable third party
edge_cases.mitigation: record the custody facts exactly as found, price the recovery attempt as a separate add-on with an honest caveat that it may not succeed, and make the launch date conditional on it rather than assuming access will appear

edge_cases.description: Half the agreed content never arrives and the client asks the operator to just write something
edge_cases.trigger: content dates pass with items outstanding
edge_cases.mitigation: park the project at the named point, move the launch date by the delay, and offer copywriting as the priced add-on it always was, while no filler text is allowed to reach the live site

edge_cases.description: The owner's adult child joins the review round late with a full redesign opinion
edge_cases.trigger: an unnamed decision-maker appears after the design was approved
edge_cases.mitigation: return to the named decision-maker rule, consolidate the new feedback into one round, and price a redesign as a change order rather than absorbing it into the build

edge_cases.description: A prospect's budget sits genuinely below the derived cost floor during an empty month
edge_cases.trigger: a below-floor deal appears when the pipeline is thin
edge_cases.mitigation: offer a smaller package rather than a smaller price, or decline; the only below-floor exception is a disclosed founding-client arrangement that buys a reference and still covers pass-through cost

edge_cases.description: A client cancels the care plan two months after a heavily subsidised build
edge_cases.trigger: early churn on a deal whose build cost was not recovered
edge_cases.mitigation: honour the cancellation and the asset handover exactly as promised, record the payback loss against the retention assumption, and change the deposit or the split for the next cohort instead of inventing an exit penalty

edge_cases.description: An older owner agrees to everything in the room and cannot repeat what recurs monthly
edge_cases.trigger: a buyer cannot evaluate or restate the offer being made to them
edge_cases.mitigation: stop, put the offer in plain writing, invite a family member or adviser to read it, and require the buyer to state the monthly cost in their own words before any signature is taken

edge_cases.description: A partner proposes a referral fee and suggests keeping it between the two of you
edge_cases.trigger: an undisclosed fee-sharing proposal from an introduction source
edge_cases.mitigation: accept only on the condition that the client is told, otherwise decline the fee and keep the reciprocal introduction; a payment the client cannot be told about is not taken

edge_cases.description: A former client asks to be removed from the portfolio after selling the business
edge_cases.mitigation: remove it promptly and without argument, replace it with a labelled demonstration or another permitted case study, and treat permission as a live condition rather than a one-time signature

edge_cases.description: The niche's referral network goes quiet after one visibly late launch
edge_cases.trigger: a delivery failure inside a tight local network
edge_cases.mitigation: repair the specific client relationship first and at the operator's cost where that is fair, lean on direct outreach and partner channels while trust rebuilds, and treat a second failure as a reason to re-read the concurrent-build capacity limit

edge_cases.description: Three clients in a row ask for online booking, which the package excludes
edge_cases.trigger: the same out-of-package request recurs across consecutive deals
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as package evidence and decide deliberately: either add a repeatable add-on with a measured build cost and its own floor, or state the exclusion earlier in the sale, but never absorb it deal by deal

edge_cases.description: A competing quote arrives at half the price promising unlimited edits and free hosting
edge_cases.trigger: a price comparison against an unbounded promise
edge_cases.mitigation: explain what the monthly fee actually covers and where the allowance ends, without disparaging the competitor, and hold the derived price; a buyer who takes the unbounded promise is postponed rather than lost

workflow.description: Commit to selling one fixed-scope build plus one monthly care plan as a single product quoted together, before any pricing or prospecting begins
workflow.gate: the package, both revenue legs and the rule for handling misfits are stated on one page

workflow.description: Answer the fit tests on repeatability, felt need, reachable local density and a reason to keep paying monthly, and name where the trade's owners gather
